posts.author: aghisays
posts.content_md:
Thanks all for the comments...

Dinesh, yes the sails are made out of some cloth but they don't move that easily but they can be moved. You can see the texture of them in the hologram it's really neat. And yes, there is a mirror behind the ship that reflects the other side of it giving it a great sense of depth. When you see it with a good light source or the sun the reflection on it is very clear.

I believe the exposure of the master was in the 20 to 30 sec range. It was done with two object beams. 

The copy exposure time was in the 45sec range. Usually my H2 copies require a long exposures (more than a minute) but I guess I'm getting better at doing masters because with this one it was "short" for me 

Thanks again for all the comments.

I'm hoping that with the EDTA bleach with ascorbic acid re-development process that I'm going to try next I can minimize it.

BTW, I've visited your website and I think your holograms are incredible. I hope one day I can get results like that.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
[quote:76fc44f530="aghisays"]Thanks Kris. 

I really like the plane hologram too. Unfurtunatelly the cockpit is made of plastic and it reflects a lot of light so I get burnin in the H2. 

I'm hoping that with the EDTA bleach with ascorbic acid re-development process that I'm going to try next I can minimize it.

[/quote:76fc44f530]

You may be able to minimise the glare by a gentle application of a mild sandpaper on the cockpit. I sometimes found that spraying shiny surfaces with hairspray kills the fresnel reflection a little. The idea is that the large particles in the aerosol scatter light making a more diffuse illumination. This doesn't always work becuase the aerosol particles aren't large enough. Also, the aerosol sometimes evaporates during the shot and so you apparently get a motion spot.
